questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Myelodysplastic syndrome is characterised by:
options: Cytopenias with a hypercellular dysplastic marrow and risk of transformation to acute leukaemia
questions.concept: MDS shows ineffective haemopoiesis - peripheral cytopenias despite a hypercellular marrow - with dysplastic changes such as ring sideroblasts, Pelger-Huet anomaly and micromegakaryocytes, and progresses to AML in about a third.
questions.reference: Robbins & Cotran 10e, Diseases of White Blood Cells

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Ring sideroblasts are demonstrated by which stain?
questions.concept: Perls stain shows iron-laden mitochondria encircling the nucleus of erythroid precursors. Ring sideroblasts occur in MDS with ring sideroblasts, lead poisoning, alcohol excess, isoniazid therapy and pyridoxine deficiency.
questions.reference: Robbins & Cotran 10e, Red Blood Cell Disorders

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Fanconi anaemia is characterised by:
options: Inherited marrow failure with chromosomal fragility, short stature and radial ray anomalies
questions.concept: Defective DNA crosslink repair causes progressive pancytopenia from about 5 to 10 years, with cafe-au-lait spots, absent or hypoplastic thumbs, renal anomalies and a high risk of AML and squamous carcinoma. Increased chromosomal breakage with diepoxybutane confirms it.
questions.reference: Robbins & Cotran 10e, Red Blood Cell Disorders

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Pure red cell aplasia with a normal white cell and platelet count following parvovirus B19 infection occurs typically in patients with:
options: Chronic haemolytic anaemia such as hereditary spherocytosis or sickle cell disease
questions.concept: Parvovirus B19 infects erythroid progenitors via the P antigen, halting erythropoiesis for about a week. This is inconsequential with a normal 120-day red cell lifespan, but precipitates aplastic crisis when the lifespan is already short.
questions.reference: Robbins & Cotran 10e, Red Blood Cell Disorders

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: The commonest cause of aplastic anaemia is:
questions.concept: Most cases are idiopathic and respond to immunosuppression with antithymocyte globulin and ciclosporin, or to stem cell transplantation in the young. Identified causes include chloramphenicol, benzene, radiation, hepatitis and pregnancy.
questions.reference: Robbins & Cotran 10e, Red Blood Cell Disorders

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Packed red cells are stored at 2 to 6 degrees Celsius for a maximum of:
options: 35 to 42 days depending on the anticoagulant preservative
questions.concept: CPDA-1 allows 35 days and additive solutions such as SAGM up to 42 days. Platelets are stored at 20 to 24 degrees with agitation for only 5 days, and fresh frozen plasma at minus 30 degrees for a year.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Leucodepletion of blood products principally reduces:
options: Febrile non-haemolytic reactions, HLA alloimmunisation and CMV transmission
questions.concept: Removing donor leucocytes prevents cytokine-mediated febrile reactions, reduces HLA sensitisation in patients needing repeated transfusion, and lowers transmission of leucocyte-associated viruses such as CMV.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: Irradiation of cellular blood products is performed to prevent:
questions.concept: Gamma irradiation inactivates donor lymphocytes, preventing transfusion-associated GVHD in immunocompromised recipients, neonates and recipients of directed donations from relatives, in whom it is almost invariably fatal.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: The mandatory screening tests for donated blood in India include all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: Indian regulations mandate screening for HIV, hepatitis B and C, syphilis and malaria. CMV screening is not routine and is reserved for selected immunocompromised recipients, for whom leucodepleted products are usually adequate.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.topic: Myelodysplasia, marrow failure & transfusion medicine
questions.stem: The window period in blood donor screening refers to:
options: The interval after infection when the donor is infectious but screening tests remain negative
questions.concept: Nucleic acid testing shortens the window period substantially compared with antibody testing, reducing but not abolishing residual transfusion transmission risk - which is why unnecessary transfusion is itself a hazard.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: The vector of dengue is:
options: Aedes aegypti, a daytime biter breeding in clean stagnant water
questions.concept: Aedes aegypti is a domestic daytime biter with a limited flight range, breeding in clean water in household containers, so source reduction and personal protection during the day are the mainstays of control.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: The warning signs in dengue that predict progression to severe disease include:
options: Persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, mucosal bleeding and a rising haematocrit with falling platelets
questions.concept: Warning signs mark the critical phase around defervescence on days 3 to 7 when plasma leakage occurs. Rising haematocrit with falling platelets indicates leakage requiring careful isotonic fluid therapy, not platelet transfusion.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: The vector of lymphatic filariasis in India is:
options: Culex quinquefasciatus, breeding in dirty polluted water
questions.concept: Culex quinquefasciatus, a night biter breeding in organically polluted water, transmits Wuchereria bancrofti which causes over 95% of Indian filariasis. Mass drug administration with DEC and albendazole is the control strategy.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: Blood samples for microfilariae in bancroftian filariasis should be collected:
options: At night, between 10 pm and 2 am, because of nocturnal periodicity
questions.concept: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae show nocturnal periodicity, appearing in peripheral blood at night coinciding with the vector's biting habit. A DEC provocation test allows daytime sampling if necessary.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) in India is transmitted by:
options: Phlebotomus argentipes sandfly, with humans as the only reservoir
questions.concept: Indian kala-azar is anthroponotic with humans as the sole reservoir, transmitted by the sandfly which breeds in cracks and crevices of mud walls. This makes elimination feasible through case detection, treatment and indoor residual spraying.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: The drug of choice for visceral leishmaniasis in the Indian elimination programme is:
questions.concept: Single-dose liposomal amphotericin B is the first-line regimen under the national programme because of widespread antimony resistance in Bihar, with miltefosine and paromomycin as alternatives.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: Post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis is important epidemiologically because:
options: Such patients act as a reservoir maintaining transmission between epidemics
questions.concept: PKDL appears months to years after apparently cured kala-azar as hypopigmented macules, nodules and plaques containing parasites, serving as a human reservoir - so its detection and treatment is central to elimination.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: Chikungunya is distinguished clinically from dengue by:
options: Severe and often prolonged incapacitating polyarthralgia with a low risk of haemorrhage or shock
questions.concept: Both are Aedes-borne with similar acute fever and rash, but chikungunya causes disabling symmetrical small joint arthralgia persisting for months, while plasma leakage, shock and marked thrombocytopenia point to dengue.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: The primary vector of malaria in rural India is:
questions.concept: Anopheles culicifacies is the main rural vector responsible for most transmission, while Anopheles stephensi is the urban vector breeding in wells, overhead tanks and construction sites. Both are night biters, hence the emphasis on bed nets.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Vector-borne disease: dengue, chikungunya, filaria, kala-azar
questions.stem: Under the national programme, the treatment of confirmed Plasmodium falciparum malaria in India is:
options: Artemisinin-based combination therapy with a single dose of primaquine as a gametocytocidal
questions.concept: ACT with single-dose primaquine on day 2 kills gametocytes and interrupts transmission. Vivax malaria instead needs chloroquine with 14 days of primaquine for radical cure after checking G6PD status.
